paragraphs.text: His purpose is to declare that man may attain in this world to various secrets of nature, but man is never able to comprehend the wisdom of God.

paragraphs.text: There is nothing but it is compassed within certain limits, and has an end, but God's wisdom.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Meaning, him that dwells by it.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: That is, come and underneath is brimstone or coal, which easily conceives fire.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: He alludes to the mines and secrets of nature, which are under the earth, into which neither souls nor beasts can enter.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: After he has declared the wisdom of God in the secrets of nature he describes his power.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Though God's power and wisdom may be understood in earthly things, yet his heavenly wisdom cannot be attained to.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: It is too high a thing for man to attain to in this world.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: It can neither be bought for gold nor precious stones, but is only the gift of God.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: Which was thought to be a king of precious stone.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: Meaning that there is no natural means by which man can attain heavenly wisdom: which he means by the souls, that fly high.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: He makes God the only author of this wisdom, and the giver of it.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: He declares that man has as much of this heavenly wisdom as he shows by fearing God and departing from evil.
